structure: Additive bivariate Gaussian random-intercept model: each measurement vector is a zero-mean stable person component plus an independent zero-mean visit deviation. The chosen within-visit deviation covariance completes one admissible scenario; the between-person covariance follows from the reported same-visit correlation.

parameter_provenance.basis: Reported variances of the stable components.

parameter_provenance.value: Independent persons; stable component independent of visit deviations; deviation vectors independent across visits.

parameter_provenance.basis: Independent stable and deviation components give variance 4 + 1 = 5 for each measurement.
Admissible scenario choice, not determined by the records; with unit deviation variances it is also the deviation correlation.
Conditional on the chosen deviation covariance, stable covariance must be 2.6 - 0.2 = 2.4.

parameter_provenance.value: Gaussian stable components and identically distributed Gaussian visit-deviation vectors
parameter_provenance.basis: Convenient sampling family; Gaussian shape is not required for the second-moment identification results.

requested_estimands.name: change_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Stable components cancel in changes. Each change has variance 2, and change covariance is twice the deviation covariance, giving correlation 0.2. The records do not identify that deviation covariance.

requested_estimands.name: same_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Directly reported by B. The model preserves it at each visit: (2.4 + 0.2)/5 = 0.52.

requested_estimands.name: cross_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Independent visit deviations leave cross-visit covariance equal to stable covariance. Under the chosen decomposition, Corr(X_visit1,Y_visit2) = 2.4/5 = 0.48; the decomposition is not identified.

limitations: This is an artificial population scenario, not biomedical validation.

Writing w for the deviation covariance, the records impose stable covariance 2.6 - w. Positive-semidefinite component covariance matrices allow every w in [-1,1]. Thus change correlation can range from -1 to 1, while cross-visit correlation ranges from 0.32 to 0.72; the two satisfy cross_visit_correlation = 0.52 - 0.2 times change_correlation.
Despite the standardized-unit labels, record C implies measurement variance 5, not 1. Measurements are not rescaled.
Finite random samples will not exactly reproduce population moments. No sample rescaling, correlation adjustment, selection, or rejection is used.
The generator has not been executed here; no Monte Carlo validation is claimed.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically verified positive definiteness: the stable covariance matrix has eigenvalues 6.4 and 1.6; the deviation covariance matrix has eigenvalues 1.2 and 0.8.
Analytically verified measurement variances of 5, same-visit covariance of 2.6, change variances of 2, change covariance of 0.4, and cross-visit covariance of 2.4.
Inspected the source for the required single generate function, seeded random sampling, one wide row per person, unique integer identifiers, and exact output column order.
